How to play

It's a stitch-by-numbers puzzle. Every number tells you how many of the nine tiles around it are light. Left-click a tile to make it light, right-click for dark.

5

Count the neighbours. This 5 means five of its 3×3 block are light — the five pale tiles, itself included.

0
9

0 means every tile around it is dark. 9 means every tile is light. These are your easiest footholds.

3

Thick gold borders split the canvas into maps. A clue only ever counts tiles inside its own map — never across a border.

1
2
3
3
1
3
2

Gold plots are sudoku — type a digit so each row, column and shape has every number once. Teal patches are picross — hover to see run-clues (lengths of light runs).

Numbers fade once satisfied and turn red if contradicted. Place every tile — light and dark — and the hidden painting is revealed. Stuck? Press H for a hint — guessing is never needed.

Advanced Deductions

On Hard and up you'll meet spots where no single clue alone fixes a tile. Compare two adjacent clues instead — especially ones 3 apart in value.

3
6

■ forced dark  ·  ■ forced light  ·  the four middle tiles are shared by both clues

The 6 and 3 overlap on the middle tiles. The 6 needs three more lights than the 3, and there are exactly three tiles only the 6 can see — so those must all be light, and the three only the 3 sees must all be dark. Forced — never a guess. Counting takes over again from there.

If in doubt, use a hint (H). Guessing is never required.

Let the needle work itself?

“This region” is the one you last stitched or typed on — solved together with any sudoku or picross it touches. The whole canvas solves region by region, skipping anything already done. The 🐞 option solves that same region but stops one square short in each puzzle — handy for testing the final-move completion.
